parsed.rationale: Both `_DequeStorage._growIfNeeded` (line 334) and `_DequeStorage._shrinkIfNeeded` (line 354) live in the same file (`Shared/Core/Sources/Core/Deque.swift`) and package (`Core`), and share a Jaccard similarity of 0.714, indicating roughly 5/7 of their token-level structure is identical. The only meaningful divergence is the direction of the capacity predicate (grow vs. shrink). Extracting a shared private helper with a capacity-condition closure would remove the duplication without changing the public or internal API surface of `_DequeStorage`.

specifics.proposed_action: Extract the shared structural skeleton of `_DequeStorage._growIfNeeded` (line 334) and `_DequeStorage._shrinkIfNeeded` (line 354) in `Shared/Core/Sources/Core/Deque.swift` into a private helper method — e.g., `_resizeIfNeeded(condition: (Int, Int) -> Bool, newCapacity: (Int) -> Int)` — and have both methods delegate to it. This eliminates the near-duplicate body (Jaccard 0.71) while preserving the distinct grow/shrink semantics at each call site.
specifics.why_no_category_fits: Neither method is a standalone generic function candidate nor a protocol default implementation. They are private storage-management helpers on the same concrete class (`_DequeStorage`) within the same file. The right fix is an internal private helper extraction — a classic 'extract method' refactor — which does not map cleanly to any of the named categories (extract-to-common targets cross-file/package duplication; generic-parameterization targets type-level generics; default-implementation targets protocol conformers). The duplication is structural (mirrored resize logic differing only in the direction of the capacity check), not coincidental.
